title: Marginal costing

titles.subject: Accounting
titles.chapter: Elements of Costing and Management Accounting

author: DkfTkX7xNnbzLCF2p
chapter_outcomes: Understand accounting for material and labour costs
Know how to identify and calculate fixed costs, variable costs, semi-variable costs and stepped costs
Know how to identify and calculate the elements of direct and indirect costs
Know how to calculate the value of closing inventory using the first in first out (FIFO) and weighted average cost (AVCO) methods (perpetual and periodic)
Understand the principles of just in time (JIT) management of inventory
Understand how to apply traditional costing methods to prepare costing statements using unit, job and batch costing principles in both manufacturing and service businesses as applicable
Evaluate the difference between a cost centre and a cost unit
Assess how to allocate and apportion overhead expenditure between production and service departments
Know how to calculate overhead absorption rates using an appropriate basis
Assess the causes and the calculation of under absorption and over absorption of overheads
Know how to prepare costing and profit statements using absorption costing
Know the uses and limitations of absorption costing
Evaluate the usefulness of absorption cost data as a support for management decision-making
Understand non-financial factors and their significance
Know how to calculate the contribution of a product
Understand how to interpret a break-even chart
Know how to calculate the break-even point, contribution to sales ratio, level of output or sales to achieve a target profit, and margin of safety
Assess the use and limitations of break-even analysis
Know how to prepare costing and profit statements using marginal costing
Know how to prepare a statement reconciling the reported profits using marginal costing and absorption costing
Assess the uses and limitations of marginal costing
Understand the usefulness of marginal costing data as a support for management decision-making, including makeor-buy, special orders, closure of business unit, limiting factors, target profit
Understand non-financial factors and their significance
Evaluate the advantages and limitations of cost–volume–profit analysis
Assess the usefulness of cost–volume–profit data as a support for management decision-making
Know how to apply costing concepts to make business decisions and recommendations using supporting data
Understand non-financial factors and their significance
